subject: BOOTAA64.EFI rebuilt on the pinned ARM64 Linux Nix builder with the #101/#102 loader patches plus one live-boot amendment
require_efi_rng_rationale: -DXNU_LOADER_REQUIRE_EFI_RNG=ON belongs to the SSH secure-boot profile (strict loader + virtio entropy device, .blauos/experiments/ssh-workflow). This image keeps the standard generic-EFI profile; the console probe attaches no entropy device, so the strict RNG requirement is not enabled.

amendment.reason: Live bisect (below) proved the original console-input loader patch silences the virtio console: its 'Virtio console RX prepared' log_info and the queue-0 notification ran between queue-enable and DRIVER_OK. vb_console_putc then posts to a queue the device is not processing, its 0.1s poll latches console_failed, and the pre-DRIVER_OK post wedges VZ's queue processing for the kernel as well. The amendment moves the queue-0 notification to just after DRIVER_OK and the RX report to after the TX-prepared line.

overlay_verification: Pinned loader + first two patches reproduce the accepted virtualbuddy-platform loader source byte-for-byte except the three files the new patches touch (include/vb_platform.h, src/devtree.c, src/vb_platform.c).

bisect_summary.method: one-change loader variants booted against the identical kernel collection and probe; guest health endpoint used to distinguish guest hang from console wedge

runs.note: guest boots; console TX dead from first byte

runs.variant: V-A notify after DRIVER_OK, RX print kept pre-DRIVER_OK
V-B no queue-0 device registers at all, RX print pre-DRIVER_OK
V-C queue 0 enabled, no posted buffer, RX print pre-DRIVER_OK
V-E allocation + 6-word property, no queue select, print pre-DRIVER_OK
V-G bare queue-select round-trip, no print
V-H full RX setup, no prints, notify after DRIVER_OK
live2 = V-H + RX report after TX-prepared line
runs.note: WORKS; serial shows both TX-prepared and RX-prepared lines

bisect_summary.conclusion: The pre-DRIVER_OK log_info virtio post is the wedge trigger; any queue-0 MMIO programming, the posted RX buffer, the extra page allocation and the 6-word property are all individually and jointly safe once printing is deferred.
bisect_summary.evidence: live/bisect/<variant>/serial.log + result.json per variant (0-byte serial = wedged console; guest health endpoint verified live guests for wedged runs)
